newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Handelsbanken has no comment on Fokus. [CORRECTED 15:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Handelsbanken has no comment on Fokus. [CORRECTED 15:50 GMT]

text.p: Swedish bank Handelsbanken declined on Friday from commenting on rumours that it would be interested in buying Norwegian bank Fokus Bank.
"We won't comment on this," a company spokesman said.
Shares in Fokus, Norway's fourth largest commercial bank, were up 5.0 crowns at 65 crowns at 1320 GMT in heavy trade.
(corrects to show share price has been higher all day).

Brokers in Oslo said there was speculation a Swedish bank would place a bid worth 70 crowns a share on Fokus, which itself is bidding to take over niche Norwegian mortgage lender Bolig og Naeringsbanken (BNbank).
A market source told Reuters that at least one major investor was contacted late on Thursday by a broker enquiring if they were willing to sell their stake and at which price.
Bjarne Borgersen, managing director at Fokus, said the sharp rise in the share price had caused a stir at the bank.

"I have heard the same rumours and it has been very hectic at the bank this morning because of the jump in our share price. I checked up the rumours and have no reason to believe that they are true," Borgersen told Reuters.

Norway's financial sector has come under the spotlight this week following the announcement on Wednesday of merger plans between the second biggest commercial bank, Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse ASA, and the country's largest insurer Storebrand ASA.
The planned merged company, Christiania Group, will be Norway's largest financial group and the sixth largest in the Nordic region.
Analysts say that as the battle for market share heats up amid slimming margins they expect further consolidation in the sector.
